test_policy.notes: UMaine is test optional for all programs; SAT/ACT are not required for admission or for merit scholarships.

requirements.notes: Apply with the Common App or the ApplyMaine application. The Apply and Application Information pages say it is free to apply; an older UMaine International Programs FAQ mentions a $50 international fee, which the current international page does not repeat. International applicants must submit a NACES-accredited transcript evaluation (exemptions: WASSCE, IB, US/Canadian schools, Cambridge International) unless waived. A school recommendation is part of a complete first-year application and an essay is recommended; Nursing applicants answer extra essay prompts.

deadlines.label: First-year Early Action (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: Completing the application and all documents by Dec. 1 gives a guaranteed decision before year end and consideration for the maximum merit scholarships (an extra $3,000 Early Action Award on the international scholarship page).

deadlines.label: Regular application deadline (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: First-year and transfer; scholarships awarded as funds are available. Admission is rolling.

deadlines.label: Final international deadline, living outside the US and Canada (fall 2027)
deadlines.notes: Later applications are reviewed on a space-available basis and most are moved to spring. The page gives no year, so 2027 is assumed for fall 2027 entry. International applicants residing in the US or Canada: final deadline Aug. 1, 2027.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Waived for native English speakers or those educated in English (listed countries incl. Canada except Quebec, Ireland, Kenya, Nigeria, UK, Australia, NZ, Ghana); 2+ years studying in the US or Canada in a non-ESL track; passing a US college English Composition course with C or higher; South African NSC English Home Language; a school letter or transcript stating English is the language of instruction for all subjects; SAT Reading/Writing 550+ or ACT English 24+. CEFR level B2 completed is also accepted. Official scores must come from the testing agency. UMaine accepts TOEFL MyBest scores.

english.notes: Minimum for tests taken before January 2026. TOEFL Essentials (not a selectable test here) needs 8.5.
Minimum for the new TOEFL (post-January 2026); the page does not name the 1-6 scale but 4.5 is listed as the post-January 2026 score.

aid.notes: International scholarships (Fall 2027) are awarded at admission from high school GPA and rigor, minimum 2.5 GPA, no extra application: Flagship Leaders Commitment $9,000-$12,000 per year, an Early Action Award of up to $3,000 more, and a Flagship Match Commitment listed at $16,200 per year (the page gives no eligibility detail). The Global Flagship Match ($25,110) is only for international students from Maine high schools. Renewable up to 4 years if GPA and credit rules are met. Need-based federal aid (FAFSA) is not available to international students; no international need-based aid is described.

cost.notes: UMaine cost of attendance 2026-27 (Orono): Maine/Canadian resident tuition $13,230; the Out-of-State and International rate is $38,340 (15 credits per semester); fees $1,070; double room plus Unlimited Flex meal plan $14,696; books $1,000; travel/misc $2,200; international students must have health insurance. Total COA $57,006 is for the out-of-state/international rate

majors.notes: Mechanical Engineering applications received after Feb. 28 are considered on a space-available basis.
Nursing applicants must answer extra written prompts (first-year) in addition to the application.
